## 開篇固定收益主論

美國財政部意外擴大長天期債券回購，在8月19日扭轉近期跌勢；即使Fed會議紀錄顯示相當多官員支持升息，漲勢仍集中在殖利率曲線最長端。30年期殖利率下跌9.2個基點至5.192%，10年期下跌5.7個基點至4.648%，5年期下跌2.4個基點至4.343%，2年期則微降0.8個基點至4.164%。

不同天期的走勢最能反映當日消息的影響。財政部才在兩週前公布維持回購規模不變的季度安排，如今表示將把10年至30年期債券的流動性支持回購規模至少提高一倍，直接紓解最容易受到財政融資、通膨不確定性及AI融資競逐資金影響的市場區段。2s30s利差因此收窄8.4個基點至102.8個基點，2s10s利差也收窄4.9個基點至48.4個基點。

10年期債券的漲勢幾乎全由實質殖利率下降帶動。10年期TIPS殖利率下跌5.6個基點至2.339%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則近乎持平於2.309%。換言之，財政部的行動降低了實質融資負擔，卻未使市場通膨補償明顯改善。Fed會議紀錄顯示，數名官員在7月主張升息，許多官員也認為，除非通膨下降，否則仍須進一步緊縮；在此背景下，兩者的區別格外重要。

交易規模也突顯這次調整的力道。FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量達$1.37兆，較前一交易日增加28.1%；名目附息債交易量增加31.5%至$1.11兆，其中20年以上券種的成交量增加52%至$1,707億，超過7年至10年期區段則增加53.1%至$2,343億。這些數據無法辨識客戶交易方向，但價格變動發生在交易活躍的市場，而非清淡的夏季盤勢。

跨資產市場將這項公告視為長期金融壓力減輕，而不是推升殖利率因素已獲解決。美元指數下跌0.82%至98.831，黃金期貨大漲4.69%至$4,570.90。20年以上美國公債指數上漲1.69%，長天期高評級公司債指數上漲約1.5%至1.6%。標普500指數上漲0.21%，但那斯達克100指數下跌0.22%，費城半導體指數重挫2.12%，顯示資本支出已成為債券供給題材一部分的科技公司仍承受壓力。

這項政策支援推出當天，美國公共債務也突破$40兆，兩者並列正好說明本輪漲勢的局限。回購可以改變投資人可取得債券的期限組合，並改善舊券交易，但無法降低政府整體融資需求。若增加國庫券籌資，部分展期與利率風險將轉向較短天期；與此同時，Fed的政策辯論仍取決於通膨能否持續回到目標，而這項條件尚未達成。

## 美國財政部鎖定長端，但未消除債務

財政部這項決定無論在時點或訊息上都不尋常。兩週前公布季度融資安排時，財政部才表示回購將維持原有規模；但在30年期殖利率升破5.30%、觸及2007年以來最高點後，財政部於季中改變安排，宣布為加強流動性支持，10年至30年期債券的購買規模將至少提高一倍。

原先時程規劃在9月9日至11月4日期間，於這些期限區段回購最多$140億；規模加倍意味著至少再增加$140億。財政部的措辭仍保留進一步擴大操作的空間，新方案將於9月9日啟動。週二一筆針對2046年至2056年到期債券的$20億回購，收到的出售報價約為目標金額的10倍，顯示持有人願意大規模把舊券售回財政部。

這項措施立即從私人投資組合中移除部分存續期間曝險，並在長端壓力升高時建立一個潛在的官方買方。30年期殖利率的跌幅接近10年期的兩倍，並超過2年期跌幅的11倍，既符合財政部鎖定的期限範圍，也反映投資人回補此前跌勢中建立的部位。

不過，相較於美國公債市場規模和政府持續舉債的流量，回購金額仍然有限。財政部並未說明如何籌措回購資金；由於其通常以國庫券因應變動性融資需求，分析師預期短期券發行量可能略為增加。富國銀行估計，若較快的回購步調延續，每季規模可能達$320億，並須在11月5日前增發約$120億國庫券，此後每季增發$160億。

與每月接近$2.25兆的國庫券總標售額相比，這些估計仍很小。自7月初以來，財政部透過國庫券淨籌資約$5,510億，其中包括8月25日交割的券種。即便如此，本次修訂仍使市場更難預期9月企業繳稅前後通常出現的國庫券供給季節性下降，也削弱財政部在再融資公告中所提供時程的參考價值。

這項措施改變的是風險分布，並未消除債務負擔。國庫券必須更頻繁地再融資，對Fed政策利率也更敏感；長天期債券雖能鎖定融資，投資人卻會要求補償通膨、財政不確定性，以及到期前價格下跌的風險。以國庫券替代部分長天期供給，可以減輕10年至30年期區段的即時壓力，卻會使未來借款成本更直接受短期利率影響。

這項取捨日益重要，因為截至週二收盤，美國公共債務已達$40.05兆，不到五年便增加三分之一；$30兆門檻則是在2022年1月才突破。距本會計年度結束尚有兩個月，利息成本已達$1.17兆，較2025年同期增加15%，規模僅次於醫療保健與社會安全支出，是第三大預算項目。

殖利率上升可能使這條路徑自我強化。再融資成本增加會推高利息支出，進一步擴大舉債需求，也可能促使投資人要求更高補償。上週10年期公債標售的融資成本為2007年以來該天期最高，30年期標售的得標殖利率則創2001年以來最高。財政部介入處理的是這項循環形成的市場價格，而不是背後的財政政策。

$41.1兆的債務上限也日益接近。惠譽預期美國將於2027年年中左右觸及上限，並在8月13日確認美國評等為AA+，同時警告決策者尚未對龐大赤字採取實質行動。然而，週三市場的即時反應仍由邊際供給主導：即使債務總額持續增加，官方承諾吸收更多長天期債券，已足以扭轉部分跌勢。

這次公告偏離固定的季度溝通，也可能衍生其他影響。投資人如今知道，當長端殖利率急升時，財政部願意調整與發債相關的操作。這可能遏止激進的空頭部位，並改善市場認定的官方壓力點附近之需求；但若通膨、赤字或公司債發行再度推升殖利率，也可能引來市場反覆測試財政部願意介入到什麼程度。

因此，當日漲勢證明的是財政部訊號的影響力，而不是殖利率下降能夠持久。若要形成持續行情，仍須私人買方願意以較低殖利率吸收新債、通膨或經濟活動降溫、競爭性發債減少，或出現可信的財政整頓；回購公告本身並未帶來其中任何一項條件。

## Fed會議紀錄顯示支持緊縮陣營更廣

Fed 7月28日至29日的會議紀錄，為長端漲勢提供了制衡。聯邦公開市場委員會以9票對3票決定把聯邦資金利率目標維持在3.5%至3.75%，這是2025年底三度降息後連續第五次按兵不動。達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan、克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack及明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari投下反對票，主張升息25個基點。

傾向收緊政策的官員不只這三名異議者。未在7月會議投票的堪薩斯城聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid與聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem後來也表示，當時會支持升息。會議紀錄指出，數名官員主張升息，許多官員則認為，若通膨未下降，便有必要進一步緊縮。

分歧主要源自物價壓力是否會持續。多數與會者預期，隨著關稅效應與先前能源價格上漲的影響消退，通膨將在今年餘下時間逐步下降；但許多人仍擔心通膨可能維持高檔更久。伊朗戰事再度升級、可能引發另一波能源衝擊，也使前景更為不明。

官員認為勞動供需大致平衡、就業市場穩定，並繼續形容經濟成長穩健，同時提及資本投資與生產力強勁。這樣的組合，使憂心通膨的決策者不必先看到勞動市場過熱，便能主張收緊政策。

會後公布的數據則讓下一次決策更難判斷。7月零售銷售創逾一年最大降幅，核心通膨溫和，雇主意外裁減職位，前兩個月的非農就業成長也遭下修。週三上午的聯邦資金期貨顯示，9月升息機率約為36%，低於7月底的逾70%。

殖利率曲線的反應反映兩個政策機關各自施力。財政部直接減輕長天期壓力，Fed會議紀錄則保留若通膨未改善便提高隔夜利率的可能性。30年期殖利率下跌逾9個基點時，2年期變動不到1個基點，顯示投資人並未因回購而抹去Fed既有的政策反應模式。

Fed主席Kevin Warsh另提議，把每年預定的政策會議由8次減至6次。他認為，約每兩個月開會一次可以累積更多資訊，也讓官員與幕僚有更多時間思考策略議題。2026年不會改變現行安排，委員會也尚未採納這項提案；但在Warsh下週首次以主席身分於傑克森洞發表演說前，提案仍增添了一項溝通議題。

會議紀錄顯示，7月維持利率不變雖獲多數支持，官員對通膨風險的判斷卻不一致。此後公布的資料顯示經濟活動與勞動市場轉弱，但中東衝突與仍偏高的通膨，使緊縮主張依然存在。財政部回購可以暫時壓低期限殖利率，卻無法決定Fed下一次會議最終將以哪一項經濟訊號為準。

## AI融資跨幣別與資本結構擴張

企業融資仍是獨立的存續期間與信用債供給來源。Alphabet首次發行澳幣債券，在接獲超過A$180億的需求後，最終規模達A$55億，高於原先考慮的約A$50億。這筆交易顯示，即使全球長期資本重新定價推高殖利率，信用實力強的借款人仍能吸引大量認購。

其中20年期券殖利率為6.98%，是Alphabet歷來任何債券的最高水準；該券發行A$10億，利差為較當地基準高180個基點。最大一檔是A$15億浮動利率債券，也是認購最踴躍的部分。不同期限與利率結構，讓投資人得以區分對科技業最強健資產負債表之一的信用曝險，以及最長天期固定利率債券所含的利率風險。

偏高的總殖利率主要反映主權利率環境，而非Alphabet信用突然惡化。美國、德國、法國、澳洲及日本的長端殖利率均升至多年高點，抬高企業借款人的基礎成本。即便絕對融資利率偏高，最終發行額仍超越初步目標，也突顯新發行人在當地市場的吸引力。

Alphabet的發債只是更大規模資金競爭的一部分。美國8月投資等級債發行額達$1,520億，創歷年同月新高，也是連續第三個月改寫單月紀錄。2026年以來，企業已發行近$1.5兆高評級債券，較上年同期增加36%。歐洲市場也在夏季淡季後異常提早恢復發行；8月前兩週僅完成€58億定價，隨後一週發行額便至少達€385億。

截至週二收盤，歐洲投資等級債利差仍接近77個基點，較6月底收窄，顯示主權債跌勢尚未演變成市場普遍拒絕為企業提供資金。相反地，政府債券基準上升，讓投資人取得更高的總殖利率；這項需求也使借款人能在主權利率再次上升並傳導至企業定價前加速交易。

AI公司與基礎設施開發商更把融資週期延伸至傳統高評級債券以外。Nebius宣布發行$45億可轉換債券，其中$27.5億於2030年到期，$17.5億於2034年到期。較短天期券行銷票息為0%至0.5%，2034年期券則為4%至4.5%；募集資金將用於興建資料中心及擴張公司的AI雲端業務。

此前Nebius今年已發行約$43億可轉換債券。反覆運用可轉債，藉由讓投資人有機會參與股權價值上升，降低部分融資的現金票息，但也使現有股東面臨稀釋。這項疑慮反映在盤前股價一度下跌9.2%；截至週二，該股原已累計上漲197%。

一項與Anthropic相關的德州計畫，顯示AI資金如何分層配置於不同資本結構。Eagle Point Credit Management為規劃中的Hubbard資料中心園區提供約$13億夾層債務；該地位於達拉斯以南約70英里。這筆貸款屬於規模$160億的專案融資方案，償付順位低於優先融資。

占地2,900英畝的園區將自建燃氣發電廠，Anthropic是主要承租人。Google為優先債務提供保證，使較大部分融資更易於安排，但夾層貸款人仍位於較後順位。工程完工後，約$150億的銀行主導融資可能以高收益債券再融資；若要採取這一步，該專案必須先取得信用評等。

這種結構也說明，評估融資負擔不能只看最大型科技公司的資產負債表。信用風險可能落在開發商、特殊目的專案、承租人、保證人或次順位貸款人身上；若工程延誤、承租人退出或再融資成本升高，究竟由哪一方負責付款，將決定融資條款。

與CoreWeave相關的融資則呈現相同問題中投機性更高的一面。高盛正試探市場對約$11.5億垃圾債券的需求，可能於9月發行，用於資助一座出租給CoreWeave的維吉尼亞州資料中心。相較於由藍籌超大型雲端業者支持的專案，投資人對依賴CoreWeave投機級信用的計畫要求更高報酬。另一筆與CoreWeave租約相關的Galaxy Digital交易，上月發行$35億債券，殖利率達10%。

Robeco的Thu Ha Chow估計，仍約有$1兆AI相關資本支出需要融資，並指出超大型雲端業者對資金價格相對不敏感。她擔心，多數融資將與主權債供給同時進入債券市場，而高評級公司債提供的利差可能吸引價格敏感型買盤離開政府債券。部分股權融資可以減輕壓力，但目前的交易管線仍持續產生大額債務融資。

週三美國公債上漲，降低了這些借款所依據的政府債券基準，卻未消除發行量，也未抹平公司債、可轉債、專案優先債務與夾層債務之間的差異。Alphabet獲超額認購的債券、Nebius的低票息可轉債，以及與Anthropic相關的次順位貸款，均透過不同管道取得資金。這些條件顯示資金仍然充裕，但融資成本與投資人保障程度會隨結構而大幅分化。

## 全球政策訊號方向分歧

美國以外的央行同樣面對能源不確定性、匯率風險與內需強弱不一的組合，但各國掌握的證據截然不同。

印尼央行在代理總裁Destry Damayanti主持的首次決策中，連續第二個月把基準利率維持在5.75%。結果符合35名經濟學家中34人的預測，也延續今年升息100個基點後的暫停。Destry強調政策延續性，表示央行仍將以穩定印尼盾為重點，同時使用其他工具支持流動性與經濟成長。

市場即時反應正面。印尼盾兌美元收高0.1%，印尼10年期公債殖利率下跌5個基點至7.11%，為近兩個月最低。Destry獲提名，加上政府提出較為節制的2027年預算，減輕前總裁Perry Warjiyo辭職造成的部分不確定性，印尼盾8月以來已上漲近1%。

政策組合正轉向誘因措施，而不是進一步推高國內殖利率。印尼央行擴大一項吸引外幣資金的避險機制，相關調整預定於9月第二週生效。Destry也表示，央行不希望SRBI證券殖利率上升。央行縮減流通餘額後，截至8月14日，12個月期SRBI平均殖利率已下跌22個基點，外資仍持續流入。

這項調整意在維持對匯率的支撐，同時減少從銀行體系抽離的流動性。7月信貸成長加速至13.58%，是至少疫情以來最快，第二季經濟成長則放緩至5.29%。印尼央行維持全年4.9%至5.7%的成長預測，也繼續把境內與境外匯市干預列為政策工具。

南非則迎來較有利的通膨意外。7月消費者物價年增4.3%，低於6月的5%及市場預測中位數4.5%；月增率也由0.7%放緩至0.2%。數據公布後，南非10年期公債殖利率下跌2個基點至8.68%，蘭特最初的漲幅則在盤中稍後消退。

物價組成令人鼓舞，但並非全面降溫。核心通膨年增率由4.1%微升至4.2%，月增率則由0.6%放緩至0.5%。食品通膨從1.4%降至0.6%，創2010年以來最低；商品通膨由4.8%放緩至3.4%，服務通膨也從5.2%降至5%。

南非央行5月升息後，7月把政策利率維持在7%，下次會議將於9月23日舉行。遠期利率協議反映再升息25個基點的機率約為70%，但這份通膨數據增強了耐心觀望的理由。高盛預期利率將維持在7%至年底，待基期效應拉低通膨後，再於2027年第一季開始降息。

澳洲央行則發出相反的警告。副總裁Andrew Hauser表示，若通膨上行風險成真、物價漲幅未能下降，澳洲央行將再度升息。央行今年前三次會議均升息，之後已連續兩次將利率維持在4.35%；最新預測顯示，通膨要到2028年初才會回到2.5%的目標。

貨幣市場反映澳洲央行在12月前再度升息的機率約為三分之二，但多數經濟學家預期今年不會再有動作。Hauser提出的條件維持了這項分歧：央行願意等待，但預測中的通膨降溫進程延後，意味著若再出現一連串不利的物價數據，緊縮可能重新啟動。

印度央行8月3日至5日會議紀錄也顯示政策帶有條件式緊縮傾向，但即時急迫性較低。六人貨幣政策委員會一致決定把附買回利率維持在5.25%，並保持中性立場。總裁Sanjay Malhotra與多數委員傾向等待通膨前景更清楚；副總裁Poonam Gupta則表示，目前沒有進一步寬鬆空間，今年稍後可能出現升息理由。

印度央行預期，10月至12月一季通膨將升至5.9%，接近容忍區間上緣；同時把截至明年3月止會計年度的經濟成長預測上調至6.7%，並把通膨預測下調至5%。這項組合使決策者仍有等待空間，但Gupta與Malhotra都指出，若食品、燃料及其他投入成本更廣泛地傳導至物價，便可能需要收緊政策。

韓國長端壓力也依然明顯。3年期與10年期公債殖利率差週二接近54個基點，為2021年10月以來最寬。自2月底以來，10年期殖利率已上升約90個基點，原因是油價與全球長天期債券壓力提高了投資人對曲線遠端所要求的補償；相較之下，3年期殖利率已較7月底高點下跌13個基點，反映投資人質疑韓國央行是否會如先前預期般積極緊縮。

阿拉伯聯合大公國決定停止與伊朗的貿易及金融交易，又增添共同的外部風險。伊朗否認應為阿聯所指的彈道飛彈攻擊負責，兩國間航班則仍持續。布蘭特原油紐約時段收高0.60%至$91.57，WTI下跌0.67%至$84.37。兩者分歧並未帶動美國通膨補償在當日普遍上升，但這場衝突仍可能破壞Fed、澳洲央行、印度央行及其他央行所依據的通膨降溫假設。

## 主權修復與私募信貸重大損失並存

新興市場信用一方面顯示部分主權資產負債表出現較持久的改善，另一方面，一宗私人企業重整卻使貸款人承受沉重損失。

埃及美元債相對美國公債的利差上週末降至322個基點，為2014年以來最低。儘管整體市場跌勢在週二推寬利差，目前水準仍較3月收窄約150個基點，並較三年前低近12個百分點。

國際貨幣基金完成審查後釋出約$18億融資，歐盟執委會也在€40億計畫下撥付€15億。僑匯、觀光收入及蘇伊士運河營收改善，共同推升埃及7月外匯存底至創紀錄的$563億。自3月底以來，埃及債券報酬率超過10%，同期整體新興市場基準僅為3.2%。

這項變化的重要性在於，它反映外部緩衝增加與IMF計畫持續執行，而不只是風險性債券普遍上漲；但埃及的資產負債表尚未完全修復。其總融資需求仍高，民營化進展有限，IMF也表示仍須維持緊縮貨幣政策、財政紀律並推動資產出售。經歷這波上漲後，部分投資人認為殖利率曲線中段與長端的價值已減少，一旦全球風險偏好惡化，也會更加脆弱。

烏克蘭債券則因另一組因素而重新定價。其美元債指數自2023年初以來累計報酬達150%，2026年以來上漲12%；2029年期債券目前交易價格接近面額的85美分，殖利率約13%，相較之下，2025年6月價格一度接近58美分。

投資人把這波復甦歸因於戰場調整能力、歐洲金融支援及債權人重整。歐洲今年稍早批准一筆€900億貸款，烏克蘭運用無人機技術也改善市場對其軍事處境的看法。其債券相對美國公債的利差已收窄至約7.4個百分點，較1月縮小約2.5個百分點。

但剩餘風險仍異常龐大。和平談判陷入停滯，飛彈短缺威脅防空能力，黑海港口遇襲可能使穀物出口減半，而債務負擔預計到2027年將達經濟產出的約110%。前國防部長Mykhailo Fedorov呼籲戰時舉行選舉，加上國會批准Yevhenii Khmara出任新任國防部長，國內政治緊張也有所升高。因此，債券上漲反映的是國家生存與取得資金的前景改善，而不是走上傳統的穩定償債道路。

在私人企業層面，MBS Group的貸款人因回收前景大幅惡化，最終轉為取得公司所有權。BlackRock旗下HPS與Oaktree Capital Management接管這家影視製作服務公司，勾銷最多$9億債務；其中HPS持有$6億第一順位抵押債權，Oaktree則持有$3億次順位抵押債權。

債權人把這些債權轉換為約$1億股權，並同意再提供$4,000萬資金，原有股東Hackman Capital Partners與Affinius Capital則失去控制權。此次重整發生前，公司面臨借款成本上升、疫情與2023年勞工罷工後影視製作活動轉弱，以及相關攝影棚資產普遍承受財務壓力。

最多$9億債務僅轉為約$1億股權，尚未計入維持公司營運所需的額外資金，已足以說明損失程度之深，並與當日順利完成的AI融資形成鮮明對比。由大型科技業承租人及保證人支持的專案資金充裕；面對設施使用率下滑的影視服務公司，其貸款人卻只能以原始債權的一小部分價值接受公司所有權。

## 前瞻市場意義

日本8月20日的20年期公債標售，是最接近的直接測試，用以觀察高殖利率能否重新吸引長天期需求。標售前20年期殖利率約為3.775%，雖低於7月3.89%的高點，仍接近歷史高位。即使日本央行可能緊縮、財政前景仍不確定，投資人將透過投標倍數與標售尾差，判斷國內買方是否願意把配置期限由5年期區段向外延伸。

政策背景使結果更具意義。隔夜指數交換顯示，日本央行9月升息的機率約為四分之三；日圓持續疲弱推升輸入型通膨，政府也支持近期採取行動。若標售需求良好，將顯示在政策路徑尚未確定前，殖利率讓利已能吸引長期資金；若結果疲弱，日本市場仍可能再次受到美國公債壓力及全球長天期資金競爭的衝擊。

瑞典央行8月20日的決策，將測試另一種條件式緊縮。受訪的19名經濟學家全數預期，政策利率將連續第七次會議維持在1.75%。關鍵在於，官員是否仍維持6月時對今年升息25個基點機率為50%的判斷，或暗示通膨風險已經上升。7月核心通膨為0.6%，高於瑞典央行預測的0.2%；但瑞典的水力與核能發電限制了能源衝擊，經濟成長也仍不均衡。

Warsh下週的傑克森洞演說，是美國政策方面的主要測試。7月會議紀錄顯示，支持緊縮的陣營比投下反對票的三人更廣，但此後的就業、零售銷售與通膨數據削弱立即行動的理由。市場需要更清楚地了解，哪些證據會促使Fed在9月升息、Fed如何區分能源衝擊與持續性的國內通膨，以及委員會是否認為長端殖利率上升所造成的金融環境緊縮具有政策效用。

財政部擴大的回購方案將於9月9日啟動。首批操作會顯示，財政部究竟只把原定金額加倍，還是運用「至少加倍」一詞所保留的彈性。配套的國庫券發行，以及未來是否調整長天期附息債標售指引，將決定實際有多少存續期間曝險從私人投資人手中移出，又有多少再融資風險轉向曲線前端。

這項方案能否持久，須與先前推升殖利率的力量相互衡量。公共債務已突破$40兆，本會計年度利息成本較一年前增加15%，AI相關借款人也持續增加長期及結構型債務。若回購後殖利率仍再度上升，財政部將面臨兩項選擇：進一步擴大介入，或讓市場重新回到自行出清的殖利率水準。

初級信用市場也將提供平行的測試。Nebius仍須為$45億可轉換債券完成定價，擬議中的CoreWeave相關維吉尼亞州融資則可能於9月帶來約$11.5億投機級債務。Alphabet澳幣長債6.98%的殖利率、Nebius透過股權轉換功能取得的低票息，以及近期CoreWeave相關債務所需的兩位數報酬，三者之間的差異將顯示投資人如何依發行人實力、擔保品與資本結構分配風險。

油價仍是各國央行決策的共同變數。阿聯中斷與伊朗的經濟往來後，布蘭特原油收在$91以上；WTI在美國時段下跌，10年期損益兩平通膨率則近乎持平。若波斯灣貿易或航運進一步受阻，能源效應將逐漸消退的假設便會受到挑戰；若運輸維持穩定、油價下降，則可強化Fed、南非央行及其他決策者耐心等待的理由，讓內需轉弱逐步傳導至通膨。

接下來，菲律賓8月27日的決策、日本央行9月18日會議，以及南非9月23日會議，將顯示各國央行面對相同外部衝擊時的反應有何差異。印尼選擇維持利率，並以匯市干預與避險誘因提供支持；澳洲與印度則明確把未來升息繫於特定條件；南非獲得有利的整體通膨意外。後續決策將決定這些路徑會繼續分歧，還是在能源壓力持續下重新匯聚至緊縮方向。

overall_summary.headline: Fed會議紀錄偏鷹，美國財政部擴大回購仍扭轉長端跌勢
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國財政部承諾把10年至30年期債券回購規模至少提高一倍，扭轉近期長端跌勢。30年期殖利率下跌9.2個基點至5.192%，10年期下跌5.7個基點至4.648%，2年期則僅微降0.8個基點至4.164%。2s30s利差收窄8.4個基點，當日美國公債交易量達$1.37兆。

10年期漲勢幾乎全由實質殖利率下降帶動：10年期TIPS殖利率下跌5.6個基點，損益兩平通膨率則近乎持平。Fed會議紀錄顯示，數名官員在7月主張升息，許多官員也預期，除非通膨下降，否則仍須進一步緊縮，因此曲線前端仍保留政策風險。回購減輕即時的長天期供給負擔，卻未降低已突破$40兆的公共債務，也未消除大規模企業與AI相關借款對資金的競爭。

市場把這項公告視為長期金融壓力減輕，美元隨之走弱、黃金急漲。股市表現分歧，半導體類股明顯下跌；與此同時，大型AI融資仍透過高評級債券、可轉債及專案債務等管道持續進行。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The US Treasury’s surprise expansion of long-maturity debt buybacks broke the recent selloff on Aug. 19, producing a rally concentrated at the far end of the curve even as Federal Reserve minutes documented substantial support for higher policy rates. The 30-year yield fell 9.2 basis points to 5.192%, the 10-year declined 5.7 basis points to 4.648%, the 5-year eased 2.4 basis points to 4.343% and the 2-year slipped 0.8 basis point to 4.164%.

That maturity pattern was the clearest expression of the day’s news. Treasury said it would at least double the size of liquidity-support buybacks involving securities in the 10- to 30-year sectors, only two weeks after publishing a quarterly schedule that left the program unchanged. The intervention offered direct relief to the part of the market most exposed to fiscal borrowing, inflation uncertainty and competition from artificial-intelligence financing. It also compressed 2s30s by 8.4 basis points to 102.8 basis points and narrowed 2s10s by 4.9 basis points to 48.4 basis points.

The 10-year rally came almost entirely through real yields. The 10-year TIPS yield fell 5.6 basis points to 2.339%, while the 10-year breakeven was nearly unchanged at 2.309%. Treasury’s action therefore reduced the real financing burden without producing a meaningful improvement in market inflation compensation. That distinction mattered after the Fed record showed several officials had favored a July rate increase and many thought tightening would be required unless inflation declined.

The scale of trading underscored the force of the adjustment. FINRA recorded $1.37 trillion of Treasury par activity, 28.1% more than the previous session. Nominal-coupon activity increased 31.5% to $1.11 trillion, with turnover in maturities above 20 years up 52% to $170.7 billion and activity in the greater-than-7-year through 10-year sector up 53.1% to $234.3 billion. The figures do not identify the direction of customer transactions, but the price move occurred in a heavily traded market rather than an inactive summer session.

Cross-asset markets treated the announcement as an easing in long-term financial pressure rather than a resolution of the forces that had driven yields higher. The US Dollar Index dropped 0.82% to 98.831, and gold futures surged 4.69% to $4,570.90. An index of Treasuries with maturities of at least 20 years gained 1.69%, while long-dated high-grade corporate-bond indexes rose about 1.5% to 1.6%. The S&P 500 advanced 0.21%, but the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.22% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 2.12%, preserving the pressure on the technology companies whose capital spending has become part of the bond-supply story.

The policy relief also arrived on the day public debt crossed $40 trillion. That juxtaposition defined the limits of the rally. Buybacks can change the maturity mix available to investors and improve trading in older securities, but they do not reduce the government’s overall financing requirement. Any reliance on additional Treasury bills would transfer part of the rollover and rate risk toward shorter maturities, while the Fed’s own debate remains conditioned on inflation that has yet to return sustainably to target.

## Treasury Targets the Long End Without Removing the Debt

Treasury’s decision was unusual in both timing and message. The department had said at its quarterly financing announcement two weeks earlier that buybacks would continue at the existing size. It then made a mid-quarter revision after the 30-year yield climbed above 5.30% and reached its highest level since 2007, saying purchases of 10- to 30-year securities would be increased by at least double to provide greater liquidity support.

The earlier schedule contemplated as much as $14 billion of buybacks in those sectors between Sept. 9 and Nov. 4. Doubling that amount would imply at least another $14 billion of purchases. The wording leaves room for larger operations, and the new program begins Sept. 9. A $2 billion operation for securities maturing from 2046 through 2056 on Tuesday had attracted offers equal to about 10 times the amount sought, showing that holders were willing to sell older bonds back to Treasury at scale.

The immediate effect was to remove some duration from private portfolios and establish a potential official buyer when long-end pressure intensifies. The 30-year yield fell nearly twice as much as the 10-year and more than 11 times as much as the 2-year. That response was consistent with the maturity range Treasury targeted and with investors covering positions built during the preceding selloff.

The amount remains modest beside the Treasury market and the underlying flow of government borrowing. Treasury did not specify how it would finance the repurchases. It ordinarily relies on bills for variable funding needs, so analysts expect the program to be accompanied by somewhat greater short-term issuance. Wells Fargo estimated that, if maintained, the faster buyback pace could reach $32 billion a quarter and require about $12 billion of additional bill issuance through Nov. 5, followed by $16 billion per quarter.

Those estimates are small beside gross bill auctions of almost $2.25 trillion each month. Treasury has already raised about $551 billion on a net basis through bill issuance since early July, including securities settling Aug. 25. Even so, the revision complicates expectations for a seasonal bill-supply decline around September corporate-tax receipts and weakens the usefulness of the schedule Treasury provided at the refunding announcement.

The action also changes the distribution of risk without retiring the debt burden. Bills require more frequent refinancing and are more sensitive to the Fed’s policy rate. Longer securities lock in funding but demand compensation for inflation, fiscal uncertainty and the possibility that their value will fall before maturity. Replacing part of the long-duration supply with bills can reduce immediate pressure on the 10- to 30-year sectors while exposing future borrowing costs more directly to short-term rates.

That tradeoff has become more important because total public debt stood at $40.05 trillion at the close of business Tuesday, one-third higher than it was less than five years ago. The $30 trillion threshold was crossed only in January 2022. With two months remaining in the fiscal year, interest costs had reached $1.17 trillion, 15% more than at the same point in 2025 and the third-largest budget category after healthcare and Social Security.

Higher yields can make that trajectory self-reinforcing. More expensive refinancing increases interest expense, which adds to borrowing needs and can lead investors to demand still more compensation. Last week’s 10-year auction carried the highest financing cost for that maturity since 2007, and the 30-year sale produced the highest award yield since 2001. Treasury’s intervention addressed the market price generated by that cycle, not the fiscal policy behind it.

The debt ceiling of $41.1 trillion is also approaching. Fitch expects it to be reached around the middle of 2027 and affirmed the US at AA+ on Aug. 13 while warning that policymakers had not taken meaningful action on large deficits. The immediate market response on Wednesday was nevertheless determined by supply at the margin: an official promise to absorb more long-duration securities was sufficient to reverse part of the selloff even though the fiscal stock continued to grow.

The announcement’s departure from regular quarterly communication may carry consequences of its own. Investors now know that Treasury is willing to adjust issuance-related operations when long yields rise sharply. That can deter aggressive short positions and improve demand near perceived official pain points. It can also invite repeated tests of how much intervention the department is prepared to undertake, especially if inflation, deficits or corporate issuance push yields higher again.

The daily rally therefore established the strength of Treasury’s signaling power, not the permanence of the yield decline. A lasting move would still require private buyers to absorb new debt at lower rates, softer inflation or activity, reduced competing issuance, or credible fiscal consolidation. None was delivered by the buyback announcement itself.

## Fed Minutes Expose a Wider Tightening Coalition

The July 28-29 Fed minutes supplied a counterweight to the long-end rally. The Federal Open Market Committee voted 9-3 to keep the federal-funds target at 3.5% to 3.75%, its fifth consecutive hold after three reductions in late 2025. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari dissented in favor of a 25-basis-point increase.

The group inclined toward tighter policy was broader than those three votes. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, neither of whom voted at the July meeting, later indicated that they also would have supported an increase. The minutes said several officials favored a hike and many thought further tightening would be necessary if inflation did not decline.

The disagreement rested largely on the persistence of price pressure. Most participants expected inflation to step down over the remainder of the year as tariff effects and earlier energy increases faded. Many, however, saw a risk that inflation would remain elevated for longer. The renewed escalation of the Iran war further clouded the outlook by threatening another energy shock.

Officials described labor demand and supply as being in balance and the labor market as stable. They continued to characterize growth as solid, while pointing to strong capital investment and productivity. That combination allowed policymakers worried about inflation to argue for tighter policy without first requiring evidence of an overheating labor market.

The data released after the meeting have made the next decision less clear-cut. July retail sales fell by the most in more than a year, core inflation was subdued, employers unexpectedly cut jobs and payroll growth in the preceding two months was revised lower. Federal-funds futures on Wednesday morning implied roughly a 36% probability of a September increase, down from more than 70% at the end of July.

The yield curve’s response reflected the different authorities acting on it. Treasury directly relieved pressure at longer maturities, while the minutes preserved the possibility that the Fed could lift the overnight rate if inflation failed to improve. The 2-year yield moved less than 1 basis point even as the 30-year fell more than 9 basis points. Investors did not treat the buyback as a reason to erase the Fed’s reaction function.

Chair Kevin Warsh also proposed reducing the number of scheduled policy meetings to six a year from eight. He argued that meetings approximately every two months would allow more information to accumulate and give officials and staff more time to consider strategic issues. No change will occur in 2026, and the committee had not adopted the proposal. Its inclusion nevertheless added another communication question before Warsh’s first Jackson Hole speech as chair next week.

The minutes clarified that July’s hold was supported by a majority but not by a unified assessment of inflation risk. The incoming evidence has since weakened activity and labor conditions, while the Middle East conflict and still-elevated inflation keep tightening arguments alive. Treasury’s buybacks can lower term yields in the meantime, but they cannot determine which of those economic signals governs the next Fed decision.

## AI Borrowing Expands Across Currencies and Capital Structures

Corporate financing remained an independent source of duration and credit supply. Alphabet completed a A$5.5 billion Australian-dollar debut, larger than the roughly A$5 billion transaction initially contemplated, after receiving more than A$18 billion of demand. The sale showed that a strong borrower can attract substantial orders while paying yields shaped by the global repricing of long-term capital.

The 20-year tranche carried a 6.98% yield, the highest Alphabet has paid on any note. It raised A$1 billion at a spread of 180 basis points over the local benchmark. The largest portion was a A$1.5 billion floating-rate note, which also attracted the most orders. The maturity mix allowed investors to separate credit exposure to one of the strongest technology balance sheets from the fixed-rate duration risk embedded in the longest bond.

The elevated all-in yield reflected the sovereign-rate backdrop more than a sudden deterioration in Alphabet’s creditworthiness. Long yields had reached multi-year highs in the US, Germany, France, Australia and Japan, raising the base cost for corporate borrowers. Yet the transaction also demonstrated the attraction of a new issuer in a local market: the final deal exceeded its initial target despite the high absolute borrowing rate.

Alphabet’s sale was part of a much larger competition for capital. US investment-grade issuance reached $152 billion for August, a record for the month and the third consecutive monthly high. Companies had sold almost $1.5 trillion of high-grade debt during 2026, 36% more than a year earlier. In Europe, issuance restarted unusually early after the summer lull, reaching at least €38.5 billion during the week after only €5.8 billion was priced in the first two weeks of August.

European investment-grade spreads remained near 77 basis points at Tuesday’s close, tighter than at the end of June, showing that the sovereign selloff had not yet translated into a broad refusal to finance companies. Investors were instead being offered higher all-in yields through the government benchmark. That demand allowed borrowers to accelerate transactions before another rise in sovereign rates reached corporate pricing.

AI companies and infrastructure developers extended the financing cycle beyond conventional high-grade bonds. Nebius announced a $4.5 billion convertible offering split between $2.75 billion due in 2030 and $1.75 billion due in 2034. The shorter securities were marketed with a 0% to 0.5% coupon, while the 2034 bonds offered 4% to 4.5%. Proceeds are intended for data-center construction and expansion of the company’s AI cloud business.

The offering follows roughly $4.3 billion of convertible issuance by Nebius earlier in the year. The repeated use of convertibles reduces the cash coupon on part of the financing by giving investors potential participation in the equity value. It also leaves existing shareholders exposed to dilution, a concern reflected in a premarket share decline of as much as 9.2% after a 197% advance through Tuesday.

A Texas project tied to Anthropic showed how AI funding is being layered across the capital structure. Eagle Point Credit Management provided about $1.3 billion of mezzanine debt for a planned data-center campus in Hubbard, roughly 70 miles south of Dallas. The loan sits within a $16 billion project-finance package and is subordinate to the senior financing.

The 2,900-acre campus will include its own gas-fired power plant, with Anthropic as the primary tenant. Google’s guarantee of the senior debt made the larger financing easier to arrange, but the mezzanine lender remains farther down the repayment hierarchy. One possible later step is a high-yield bond refinancing of the roughly $15 billion bank-led portion after construction, which would require the project to obtain a credit rating.

That structure illustrates why the financing burden cannot be assessed solely from the balance sheets of the largest technology companies. Credit risk can reside with a developer, a special-purpose project, a tenant, a guarantor or a subordinated lender. The credit terms depend on which party must make payments if construction is delayed, the tenant withdraws or refinancing becomes more expensive.

CoreWeave-linked financing presented a more speculative version of the same issue. Goldman Sachs was gauging demand for about $1.15 billion of junk bonds, potentially in September, to fund a Virginia data center leased to CoreWeave. Investors have demanded higher returns from projects supported by CoreWeave’s speculative-grade credit than from those backed by blue-chip hyperscalers. A separate Galaxy Digital transaction tied to a CoreWeave lease paid a 10% yield on $3.5 billion last month.

Robeco’s Thu Ha Chow estimated that roughly $1 trillion of AI-related capital spending still needs funding and said hyperscalers have been relatively insensitive to its price. Her concern is that much of the financing will arrive in bond markets alongside sovereign issuance, with highly rated corporate spreads drawing price-sensitive buyers away from government debt. Some equity financing could reduce that pressure, but the current pipeline continues to produce large debt transactions.

Wednesday’s Treasury rally eased the government benchmark underlying that borrowing. It did not remove the volume of issuance or the distinctions among corporate, convertible, senior-project and mezzanine risk. Alphabet’s oversubscribed deal, Nebius’s low-coupon convertibles and the Anthropic-linked subordinated loan all found financing through different channels. Their terms show that capital remains available, but its cost and protection vary sharply according to structure.

## Global Policy Signals Pull in Different Directions

Central banks outside the US confronted the same combination of energy uncertainty, currency risk and uneven domestic demand with markedly different evidence.

Bank Indonesia held its benchmark rate at 5.75% for a second month in the first decision led by acting Governor Destry Damayanti. The outcome matched the forecasts of 34 of 35 economists and extended the pause after 100 basis points of increases this year. Destry emphasized continuity and said policy would remain focused on rupiah stability while the bank used other instruments to support liquidity and growth.

The immediate market response was constructive. The rupiah finished 0.1% stronger against the dollar, and Indonesia’s 10-year government yield fell 5 basis points to 7.11%, its lowest in almost two months. The currency had gained nearly 1% in August as Destry’s nomination and the government’s restrained 2027 budget reduced some of the uncertainty created by former Governor Perry Warjiyo’s resignation.

The policy mix is shifting toward incentives rather than still-higher domestic yields. Bank Indonesia expanded a hedging scheme intended to attract foreign currency, with the changes scheduled to take effect in the second week of September. Destry also signaled that the bank did not want yields on its SRBI securities to rise. The average 12-month SRBI yield had fallen 22 basis points by Aug. 14 after the bank reduced the amount outstanding, while foreign inflows continued.

That adjustment is intended to preserve currency support without draining as much liquidity from banks. Credit growth accelerated to 13.58% in July, the fastest pace since at least the pandemic, while Q2 economic growth slowed to 5.29%. Bank Indonesia maintained a 4.9% to 5.7% full-year growth forecast and retained intervention in both onshore and offshore currency markets as part of its toolkit.

South Africa received a more favorable inflation surprise. Consumer prices rose 4.3% from a year earlier in July, down from 5% in June and below the 4.5% median forecast. Monthly inflation slowed to 0.2% from 0.7%. The 10-year government yield fell 2 basis points to 8.68% after the release, while the rand’s initial gain faded later in the session.

The composition was encouraging but not uniformly softer. Core inflation edged up to 4.2% annually from 4.1%, although its monthly pace slowed to 0.5% from 0.6%. Food inflation dropped to 0.6% from 1.4%, its lowest since 2010, and goods inflation decelerated to 3.4% from 4.8%. Services inflation eased to 5% from 5.2%.

The South African Reserve Bank held its policy rate at 7% in July after raising it in May and next meets on Sept. 23. Forward-rate agreements assigned about a 70% probability to another 25-basis-point increase, but the inflation release strengthened the case for patience. Goldman Sachs expects the rate to remain at 7% through year-end before cuts begin in Q1 2027 as base effects pull inflation lower.

Australia’s central bank delivered the opposite warning. Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the Reserve Bank would raise rates again if upside inflation risks materialized and price growth failed to decline. The RBA had left its rate at 4.35% for a second meeting after raising it at the first three meetings of the year. Its latest forecasts do not show inflation returning to the 2.5% target until early 2028.

Money markets assigned roughly a two-in-three probability to another Australian increase by December, although most economists expected no further move this year. Hauser’s condition preserved that divergence: the central bank is willing to wait, but the delay in projected disinflation means another unfavorable price sequence could restart tightening.

Minutes from India’s Aug. 3-5 meeting revealed a similar conditional bias with less immediate urgency. The Reserve Bank of India’s six-member committee unanimously held the repurchase rate at 5.25% and retained a neutral stance. Governor Sanjay Malhotra and most colleagues favored waiting for more clarity on inflation, while Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said there was no present scope for further easing and that a case for a hike could emerge later in the year.

The RBI expects inflation to reach 5.9% in the October-December quarter, close to the upper end of its tolerance band. It raised its growth forecast for the fiscal year through March to 6.7% and lowered its inflation forecast to 5%. The combination gives policymakers room to wait, but Gupta and Malhotra both identified broader pass-through from food, fuel and other inputs as a condition that could require tightening.

Long-end pressure also remained visible in Korea. The gap between 3- and 10-year government yields reached almost 54 basis points on Tuesday, its widest since October 2021. The 10-year yield had risen about 90 basis points since the end of February as oil and global duration pressure increased the compensation required farther out the curve. The 3-year yield, by contrast, had fallen 13 basis points from its late-July high as investors questioned whether the Bank of Korea would tighten as aggressively as previously expected.

The UAE’s decision to halt trade and financial transactions with Iran added to the common external risk. Iran denied responsibility for the ballistic-missile attack cited by the UAE, and flights between the countries continued. Brent finished the New York session 0.60% higher at $91.57, while WTI declined 0.67% to $84.37. The divergence did not produce a broad daily rise in US inflation compensation, but the conflict remains capable of disrupting the disinflation assumptions used by the Fed, RBA, RBI and other central banks.

## Sovereign Repair Coexists With Severe Private-Credit Losses

Emerging-market credit produced evidence of durable improvement in some sovereign balance sheets even as a private restructuring imposed deep losses on lenders.

Egypt’s dollar-bond spread over Treasuries reached 322 basis points at the end of last week, its lowest since 2014. Although the broader market selloff pushed the spread wider on Tuesday, it remained about 150 basis points tighter than in March and nearly 12 percentage points below its level three years ago.

The improvement followed an IMF review that unlocked about $1.8 billion of financing and a €1.5 billion European Commission disbursement under a €4 billion program. Remittances, tourism and improved Suez Canal receipts helped lift foreign-currency reserves to a record $56.3 billion in July. Egyptian bonds returned more than 10% from the end of March, compared with 3.2% for the broader emerging-market benchmark.

The shift is significant because it reflects larger external buffers and continued implementation of the IMF program rather than only a generalized rally in risky debt. It is not complete balance-sheet repair. Egypt still has high gross financing needs and has made limited progress on privatization, while the IMF has said tight monetary policy, fiscal discipline and divestments remain necessary. After the rally, some investors see less value in the middle and long portions of the curve and greater vulnerability to a global deterioration in risk appetite.

Ukraine’s bonds have repriced for a different set of reasons. An index of its dollar debt has returned 150% since the start of 2023 and 12% during 2026, with the country’s 2029 notes trading near 85 cents on the dollar and yielding about 13%. They had traded near 58 cents in June 2025.

Investors attributed the recovery to battlefield adaptation, European financial support and creditor restructurings. Europe approved a €90 billion loan earlier in the year, while Ukraine’s use of drone technology improved perceptions of its military position. The spread over Treasuries narrowed to about 7.4 percentage points, roughly 2.5 points tighter than in January.

The remaining risks are unusually large. Peace talks have stalled, missile shortages threaten air defenses, attacks on Black Sea ports could halve grain exports and the debt burden is expected to reach about 110% of economic output by 2027. Domestic political tension also increased after former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for wartime elections and lawmakers approved Yevhenii Khmara as the new defense minister. The bond rally reflects improved survival and funding prospects, not a conventional path toward stable debt service.

At the private-company level, MBS Group’s lenders converted a much weaker recovery outlook into ownership. BlackRock’s HPS and Oaktree Capital Management took control of the entertainment-production services company, wiping out as much as $900 million of debt. HPS held a $600 million first lien and Oaktree a $300 million junior lien.

The creditors converted those claims into about $100 million of equity and agreed to provide another $40 million. Existing owners Hackman Capital Partners and Affinius Capital were displaced. The restructuring followed higher borrowing costs, weaker film and television production after the pandemic and the 2023 labor strikes, and financial strain across related studio properties.

The roughly $100 million equity conversion against as much as $900 million of debt demonstrates the severity of the loss even before considering the additional capital needed to keep the business operating. It also stands apart from the day’s successful AI financings. Capital was abundant for projects supported by large technology tenants and guarantees, while lenders to an entertainment-services company facing weaker utilization accepted ownership at a fraction of their original claims.

## Forward Market Significance

Japan’s 20-year government-bond auction on Aug. 20 is the nearest direct test of whether elevated yields can restore demand for duration. The 20-year yield entered the sale near 3.775%, below July’s 3.89% peak but still close to historically high levels. Investors will assess the bid-to-cover ratio and auction tail for evidence that domestic buyers are prepared to extend beyond the 5-year sector despite prospective Bank of Japan tightening and fiscal uncertainty.

The policy backdrop makes the result more consequential. Overnight-indexed swaps assigned about a three-quarters probability to a BOJ increase in September, and the government has supported a near-term move as persistent yen weakness adds to imported inflation. A well-received auction would show that yield concessions are drawing long-term demand even before the policy path is settled. A weak result would leave Japan exposed to renewed pressure from US Treasuries and the global competition for duration.

The Riksbank’s Aug. 20 decision will test another form of conditional tightening. All 19 economists surveyed expect Sweden’s policy rate to remain at 1.75% for a seventh meeting. The issue is whether officials retain their June assessment of a 50% probability of a 25-basis-point increase this year or indicate that inflation risks have increased. Core inflation reached 0.6% in July against the Riksbank’s 0.2% forecast, but Sweden’s hydro and nuclear generation has limited the energy shock and growth remains uneven.

Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech next week carries the central US policy test. The July minutes showed a wider tightening coalition than the three recorded dissenters, but subsequent employment, retail and inflation data weakened the case for immediate action. Markets will need a clearer account of what evidence would prompt a September increase, how the Fed distinguishes an energy shock from persistent domestic inflation and whether long yields are tightening financial conditions in a way the committee considers useful.

Treasury’s expanded buybacks begin Sept. 9. The first operations will show whether the department merely doubles the previously scheduled amounts or exercises the flexibility implied by “at least” double. Associated bill issuance and any future change to long-coupon auction guidance will determine how much duration is actually transferred away from private investors and how much refinancing risk moves toward the front end.

The program’s durability will be judged against the forces that preceded it. Public debt has crossed $40 trillion, fiscal-year interest costs are 15% higher than a year ago and AI-related borrowers continue to add long-term and structured obligations. If yields rise again despite the purchases, Treasury would face a choice between enlarging the intervention and allowing market clearing levels to reassert themselves.

Primary credit markets will supply a parallel test. Nebius still has to price its $4.5 billion convertible sale, while the proposed CoreWeave-linked Virginia financing may bring about $1.15 billion of speculative-grade debt in September. The difference between Alphabet’s 6.98% long Australian yield, the low coupons available through Nebius’s equity conversion feature and the double-digit return recently required on CoreWeave-linked debt will show how investors distribute risk across issuer strength, collateral and capital structure.

Oil remains the common variable across central-bank decisions. Brent ended above $91 as the UAE severed economic ties with Iran, while WTI declined during the US session and the 10-year breakeven was nearly unchanged. A further disruption to Gulf trade or shipping would challenge the assumption that energy effects will fade. Stable flows and lower crude prices would strengthen the case for the Fed, South African Reserve Bank and other policymakers to wait while weaker domestic demand works through inflation.

The Aug. 27 Philippine decision, the Sept. 18 BOJ meeting and South Africa’s Sept. 23 meeting will then show how differently central banks respond to that external shock. Indonesia has chosen a rate hold supported by currency intervention and hedging incentives; Australia and India have kept future increases explicitly conditional; South Africa has received a favorable headline inflation surprise. The next decisions will determine whether those paths remain distinct or converge toward renewed tightening if energy pressure persists.

section_summaries.market_read: The rally came through real yields, not lower inflation compensation, while the front end retained the Fed’s tightening risk.
section_summaries.summary: Treasury’s surprise buyback expansion produced a heavily traded rally concentrated at the long end, with the 30-year yield falling much more than the 2-year. The move reduced real financing costs and flattened the curve, but stable inflation compensation, hawkish Fed minutes and public debt above $40 trillion limited the signal to relief from duration pressure rather than a resolution of fiscal or inflation risk.

section_summaries.market_read: Buybacks can improve long-end liquidity and alter maturity supply, but lasting yield relief still requires sustained private demand.
section_summaries.section_title: Treasury Targets the Long End Without Removing the Debt
section_summaries.summary: Treasury reversed guidance issued only two weeks earlier and said 10- to 30-year liquidity-support buybacks would at least double from Sept. 9. The official bid removed duration at the margin and deterred short positions, but the purchases remain small beside government borrowing. Financing them with more bills would shift refinancing and policy-rate exposure toward the front end without reducing the debt stock.

section_summaries.market_read: The muted 2-year move showed that investors did not treat Treasury’s buybacks as a change to the Fed’s reaction function.
section_summaries.section_title: Fed Minutes Expose a Wider Tightening Coalition
section_summaries.summary: The Fed held rates at 3.5% to 3.75% by a 9-3 vote, but the minutes showed the tightening coalition extended beyond the dissenters: several officials favored an increase and many saw one as necessary if inflation failed to decline. Softer jobs, retail and core-inflation data since the meeting have reduced the implied chance of a September move, while energy risk keeps the debate unresolved.

section_summaries.market_read: Sovereign yields set a higher base cost, while convertibility, guarantees and seniority redistributed credit risk across investors.
section_summaries.next_check: Nebius pricing and a possible September CoreWeave-linked junk deal will test demand across financing structures.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowing Expands Across Currencies and Capital Structures
section_summaries.summary: AI financing expanded across high-grade bonds, convertibles and project debt. Alphabet’s A$5.5 billion debut drew more than A$18 billion of demand despite a 6.98% yield on its 20-year tranche; Nebius launched $4.5 billion of convertibles; and an Anthropic-linked campus received $1.3 billion of mezzanine financing. Capital remains available, but cost and protection vary sharply by issuer, collateral and repayment rank.

section_summaries.market_read: Domestic inflation and currency conditions are producing different policy paths despite a common external energy risk.
section_summaries.next_check: Further disruption to Gulf trade or shipping would test whether central banks can continue waiting for domestic inflation to ease.
section_summaries.section_title: Global Policy Signals Pull in Different Directions
section_summaries.summary: Bank Indonesia held at 5.75% while supporting the rupiah through intervention and new hedging incentives. Softer South African inflation strengthened the case for patience, but Australia retained an explicit tightening warning and India identified broader cost pass-through as a possible reason to raise rates later. Divergent Brent and WTI moves left the Iran conflict as a shared threat to disinflation assumptions.

section_summaries.market_read: Improved sovereign buffers supported repricing, while MBS showed how weak utilization and high borrowing costs can erase junior value.
section_summaries.section_title: Sovereign Repair Coexists With Severe Private-Credit Losses
section_summaries.summary: Egypt’s stronger reserves and multilateral funding and Ukraine’s external support have driven substantial sovereign-bond recoveries, though both retain large financing and political risks. In private credit, MBS Group’s lenders took control after converting as much as $900 million of debt into about $100 million of equity, illustrating how severe losses can coexist with abundant financing for stronger or better-protected borrowers.

Japan’s Aug. 20 20-year auction will test demand for global duration, and Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech must clarify the threshold for a September Fed increase. Treasury’s Sept. 9 buyback launch will reveal the scale of duration transfer and related bill issuance. Oil disruption, pending AI financings and later central-bank meetings will test whether easing long-end pressure can persist against inflation and supply risks.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury buyback expansion breaks the long-end selloff despite hawkish Fed minutes
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasury’s promise to at least double buybacks of securities in the 10- to 30-year sectors reversed the recent long-end selloff. The 30-year yield fell 9.2 basis points to 5.192%, the 10-year declined 5.7 basis points to 4.648%, and the 2-year slipped just 0.8 basis point to 4.164%. The move flattened 2s30s by 8.4 basis points and occurred amid $1.37 trillion of Treasury activity.

The 10-year rally came almost entirely through real yields: the 10-year TIPS yield fell 5.6 basis points while the breakeven was nearly unchanged. Fed minutes showed several officials favored a July increase and many expected further tightening unless inflation declined, preserving front-end policy risk. Buybacks eased the immediate duration burden but did not reduce public debt, which crossed $40 trillion, or eliminate competition from heavy corporate and AI-related borrowing.

The dollar weakened and gold surged as markets treated the announcement as relief from long-term financial pressure. Equities were mixed, with semiconductors falling sharply, while large AI financings continued across high-grade bonds, convertibles and project debt.
overall_summary.summary: Long-end Treasuries rallied after an unexpected expansion of liquidity-support buybacks, lowering real yields and flattening the curve even as Fed minutes showed broad support for tighter policy if inflation remains elevated.
